artists.biography: Santana is an American rock band formed in San Francisco, California, in 1966 by Mexican-American guitarist Carlos Santana. The band has had various recording and performing line-ups in its history, with Santana being the only consistent member. After signing with Columbia Records, the band's appearance at the Woodstock Festival in 1969 increased their profile and they went on to record the critically acclaimed and commercially successful albums Santana (1969), Abraxas (1970) and Santana III (1971). These were recorded by the group's "classic" line-up, comprising organist and lead vocalist Gregg Rolie, percussionists José "Chepito" Areas and Michael Carabello, drummer Michael Shrieve and bassist David Brown. Hit songs of this period include "Evil Ways" (1970), "Black Magic Woman" (1970), "Oye Como Va" (1971) and the instrumental "Samba Pa Ti" (1970).

perplexity.description:
Santana's Greatest Hits, released in July 1974 by Columbia Records, is a compilation album that captures the band's most influential early work from 1969 to 1971. Musically, the album showcases Santana's signature blend of rock, Latin rhythms, jazz fusion, and blues, marked by Carlos Santana's distinctive guitar playing and the group's dynamic percussion section. The collection features iconic tracks such as "Evil Ways," "Black Magic Woman," "Oye Como Va," and "Soul Sacrifice," which exemplify the band's ability to merge rock energy with Afro-Cuban and jazz influences.

This album holds a pivotal place in Santana's discography as their first greatest hits compilation, arriving after the success of their debut album Santana (1969) and the landmark Abraxas (1970). It served as a concise introduction to the band's sound for new listeners and a definitive summary for fans. Commercially, Santana's Greatest Hits became the band's best-selling compilation, achieving multi-platinum status in the United States and earning gold and platinum certifications in several other countries. The album's enduring popularity and critical acclaim underscore its significance as a cornerstone of Santana's legacy and a classic example of 1970s rock fusion.
